# `secrets/provider-key-test`: Hardcoded test-mode API key

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:rules` from the rule metadata in src/rules/. Edit only the
     hand:* regions here; everything else comes from the rule and is overwritten. -->

| Family  | Default severity | GitHub security-severity | CWE                                                        |
| ------- | ---------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| secrets | low              | 2.5                      | [CWE-798](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html) |

Individual findings can have a lower or higher severity than the default, and each has a
confidence (high, medium or low). Both are explained below.

## What it detects

<!-- hand:detects -->

Stripe test-mode secret and restricted keys (`sk_test_…`, `rk_test_…`) written literally in
a scanned file. Same matching, placeholder and file rules as
[`secrets/provider-key`](provider-key.md), but a separate rule id with **low** severity,
so tools that rank by rule (GitHub code scanning) do not show a test key as critical.

<!-- /hand:detects -->

## Why it matters

A test-mode secret key (for example Stripe sk_test_…) is written in the code. It cannot move real money, but it grants full API access to your test account: test customers, webhooks, settings and logs. Test keys are often swapped for live keys in the same place, which is how live keys end up committed.

## Messages

What a finding from this rule says (parameters in braces):

- {provider} is hardcoded. Test-mode keys cannot move real money but still grant API access to your account’s test data and settings.

## How to fix

Load test keys from the environment exactly like live keys, so that switching to live never means editing code. Roll the test key in the dashboard if the repository is shared or public.

### Vulnerable

```ts
const stripe = new Stripe('sk_test_…'); // "only a test key", until it becomes sk_live_
```

### Fixed

```ts
const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY!); // sk_test_ locally, sk_live_ in production
```

## False positives and limitations

<!-- hand:false-positives -->

- A test key cannot move real money, so the severity is low. It still grants full API
  access to the account's test data, webhooks and settings, and it often sits exactly
  where the live key will be pasted later.
- If the test key is intentional (for example in a public demo project), suppress it with
  that reason, or set the rule to `off` in `.vibeguard.yml`.
- Publishable keys (`pk_test_…`, `pk_live_…`) are public by design and never reported.

<!-- /hand:false-positives -->

## How to suppress

Only suppress a finding after confirming it is safe. Put the directive on the line above
the reported line (or use `vibeguard-ignore-line` on the line itself, or
`vibeguard-ignore-file` anywhere in the file). The reason is required: a directive without
one suppresses nothing and is reported.

```ts
// vibeguard-ignore-next-line secrets/provider-key-test -- explain why this is safe (at least 10 characters)
<the line VibeGuard reported>
```

Use the comment syntax of the file: `//` or `/* */` in code, `#` in `.env` and YAML
files, `--` in SQL.

To turn the rule off or change its severity for the whole project, use `.vibeguard.yml`:

```yaml
version: 1
rules:
  secrets/provider-key-test: off # or: { severity: low }
```

See [configuration](../../configuration.md) and
[ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-suppression-design.md).

## CWE

- [CWE-798](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html): Use of Hard-coded Credentials
